name: Markov decision process formalism
definition: Bellman's mathematical framework of states, actions, transition probabilities and rewards for sequential decision-making under uncertainty.
causal_claim: Markov decision process formalism made the modern AI agent possible by defining the mathematical object an acting agent optimizes: a policy over states and actions with cumulative reward.

name: Q-learning
definition: Watkins' model-free reinforcement learning algorithm that learns the value of state-action pairs from experience without a model of the environment.
causal_claim: Q-learning made the modern AI agent possible by proving an agent can learn what to do purely from reward signals, the learning-from-feedback lineage that RLHF later adapted for language models.
source_title: Learning from Delayed Rewards (thesis, University of Cambridge)

name: Temporal difference learning
definition: Sutton's method of learning predictions by bootstrapping from later predictions, the core update rule of modern reinforcement learning.
causal_claim: Temporal difference learning made the modern AI agent possible by supplying the bootstrapped value-learning mechanism underlying the reinforcement methods used to align and steer agent behavior.
source_title: Learning to Predict by the Methods of Temporal Differences

name: Monte Carlo tree search
definition: A search algorithm that builds a decision tree guided by random simulation outcomes, famously powering AlphaGo's move selection.
causal_claim: Monte Carlo tree search made the modern AI agent possible by demonstrating that learned models plus lookahead search produce superhuman sequential decisions, the planning pattern agent architectures imitate.

name: Statistical learning theory (VC dimension)
definition: Vapnik and Chervonenkis's theory bounding generalization error by a capacity measure of a hypothesis class, founding the mathematics of learning from data.
causal_claim: Statistical learning theory (VC dimension) made the modern AI agent possible by first making 'learning from finite data' a rigorous science, the intellectual frame in which training a model to generalize is understood.

name: Universal approximation theorem
definition: Cybenko's proof that a feedforward network with a single hidden layer can approximate any continuous function on a compact set.
causal_claim: Universal approximation theorem made the modern AI agent possible by guaranteeing that neural networks are expressive enough in principle to represent the mappings agents need, justifying the bet on scale.
source_title: Approximation by superpositions of a sigmoidal function

name: Stored-program architecture
definition: The von Neumann design in which instructions and data share one memory, making the computer a universal, reprogrammable machine.
causal_claim: Stored-program architecture made the modern AI agent possible by creating the general-purpose computer on which every model, tool and agent loop physically runs.
source_title: First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC

name: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge (ILSVRC)
definition: An annual computer vision competition (2010-2017) evaluating algorithms on ImageNet object detection and classification tasks.
causal_claim: The ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge made the modern AI agent possible by creating the annual benchmark competition whose 2012 result demonstrated deep learning's superiority and redirected the field.

name: GLUE benchmark
definition: The General Language Understanding Evaluation benchmark, a collection of nine sentence- and sentence-pair understanding tasks for training and evaluating NLP models.
causal_claim: GLUE benchmark made the modern AI agent possible by giving language models a shared measurable target for general understanding, driving the encoder era whose models agents now build on.

name: Tensor processing unit (TPU)
definition: Google's custom ASIC designed to accelerate machine learning workloads, first used internally in 2015 and announced in 2016.
causal_claim: The tensor processing unit made the modern AI agent possible by showing custom silicon for tensor algebra could cut the cost of training and serving large neural networks by an order of magnitude.

name: Amazon Web Services
definition: Amazon's cloud computing platform, launched in 2006 with S3 and EC2, offering on-demand compute and storage over the internet.
causal_claim: Amazon Web Services made the modern AI agent possible by making elastic compute rentable by the hour, so training runs and agent hosting no longer required owning a data center.

name: Git
definition: Linus Torvalds' distributed version control system, created in 2005 for Linux kernel development.
causal_claim: Git made the modern AI agent possible by becoming the version control substrate of the open-source ecosystem whose code and collaboration produced the frameworks agents are built with.

name: GitHub
definition: A web-based platform for version control and collaborative software development built on Git, launched in 2008.
causal_claim: GitHub made the modern AI agent possible by centralizing open-source collaboration, hosting the code, issues, and training corpora that the agent ecosystem is built from.

name: Point-contact transistor
definition: The first working transistor, demonstrated by Bardeen and Brattain at Bell Labs in December 1947 using a germanium point-contact design.
causal_claim: The point-contact transistor made the modern AI agent possible by replacing vacuum tubes with a solid-state switch, the device from which all digital computing hardware descends.

name: Silicon transistor
definition: The first silicon transistor, produced by Gordon Teal at Texas Instruments in 1954, replacing fragile germanium devices.
causal_claim: The silicon transistor made the modern AI agent possible by making transistors cheap, rugged, and manufacturable, turning computing hardware into a mass-produced commodity.

name: Planar process
definition: Jean Hoerni's 1957-1959 process of building transistors under a protective silicon oxide layer on a flat wafer surface.
causal_claim: The planar process made the modern AI agent possible by making transistors printable in batches on a flat wafer, the manufacturing step that let chips scale.

name: Integrated circuit
definition: A set of electronic circuits on one small flat piece of semiconductor material, independently demonstrated by Kilby (1958) and Noyce (1959).
causal_claim: The integrated circuit made the modern AI agent possible by putting whole circuits on one chip, collapsing cost and size so computing could scale for decades.

name: Czochralski process
definition: A method of crystal growth, adapted to silicon in the 1950s, that pulls a large single crystal from molten material using a seed crystal.
causal_claim: The Czochralski process made the modern AI agent possible by supplying the large, near-perfect silicon single crystals from which virtually all semiconductor wafers are cut.

name: Zone refining
definition: William Pfann's technique of passing molten zones along a rod to sweep impurities to one end, purifying semiconductor material.
causal_claim: Zone refining made the modern AI agent possible by achieving the ultra-pure semiconductor material without which reliable transistors cannot be made.

name: MOSFET
definition: The metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor, demonstrated by Kahng and Atalla at Bell Labs in 1959 and now the most manufactured device in history.
causal_claim: The MOSFET made the modern AI agent possible by becoming the scalable, low-power switch of which modern processors and AI accelerators contain tens of billions.

name: Photolithography
definition: A process using light to transfer a geometric pattern from a photomask to a light-sensitive chemical photoresist on a substrate.
causal_claim: Photolithography made the modern AI agent possible by providing the printing technique that shrinks transistor features generation after generation.

name: Probability axioms (Kolmogorov)
definition: Andrey Kolmogorov's 1933 axiomatization of probability theory on measure-theoretic foundations in 'Foundations of the Theory of Probability'.
causal_claim: Probability axioms (Kolmogorov) made the modern AI agent possible by giving uncertainty a rigorous calculus on which statistical learning and probabilistic model outputs rest.
source_title: Foundations of the Theory of Probability - Wikipedia

name: Linear algebra (matrix calculus)
definition: The body of linear algebra (vectors, matrices, transformations) formalized in the 19th-20th centuries and used to express computation in modern computing.
causal_claim: Matrix calculus and linear algebra made the modern AI agent possible by supplying the mathematical language in which neural network computation is expressed as tensor operations.

name: Gradient descent
definition: A first-order iterative optimization algorithm for finding a local minimum of a differentiable function, rooted in Cauchy's 1847 method.
causal_claim: The gradient descent algorithm made the modern AI agent possible by giving an iterative rule for minimizing a loss function, the engine of all neural network training.

name: Monte Carlo method
definition: A class of computational algorithms relying on repeated random sampling, developed by Ulam, von Neumann, and Metropolis in the 1940s.
causal_claim: Monte Carlo method made the modern AI agent possible by showing intractable integrals and expectations could be estimated by random sampling, a technique used throughout training and evaluation.

name: Boolean algebra
definition: George Boole's 1854 'An Investigation of the Laws of Thought', introducing an algebraic system of logic with true/false values.
causal_claim: Boolean algebra made the modern AI agent possible by reducing logic to algebra, the formal basis on which digital circuits and computation are built.

name: ARPANET
definition: The first wide-area packet-switched network with distributed control, first deployed in 1969, and a direct predecessor of the internet.
causal_claim: ARPANET made the modern AI agent possible by proving packet-switched networking worked, creating the network lineage that became the internet agents operate over.

name: TCP/IP
definition: The Internet protocol suite, designed by Cerf and Kahn in 1974 and adopted as the ARPANET standard on January 1, 1983.
causal_claim: TCP/IP made the modern AI agent possible by standardizing how networks interoperate, creating the single global network through which agents perceive and act.

name: World Wide Web
definition: Tim Berners-Lee's 1989-1991 system of interlinked hypertext documents accessed via the internet, built at CERN.
causal_claim: World Wide Web made the modern AI agent possible by creating the hyperlinked document space that became both the largest text corpus for training and the environment agents browse and act in.
